- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.22 or below) in recent days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecasted decline, reduce the peak value by 5–15% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If true outcome shows a strong downward trend after a recent peak, model tends to overcorrect — adjust forecast to be 3–5% lower than predicted peak.  
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending down, model often overreacts — reduce forecasted highs by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of sentiment are negative, apply a downward bias of 3–7% to the final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 7–10 days), reduce those values by 5–10% to align with observed lag in price reaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate volatility — cap forecast variance within ±3% of recent 7-day average.
